rv.q: This show, evocatively designed by Christopher Oram, is something new, weird and gutsy enough to jettison most conventional expectations.
Ghee as The Lady Chablis is the real beating heart in MIDNIGHT OF THE GARDEN OF GOOD AND EVIL, but otherwise the musical's score and character arcs need refinement to really come into focus.
This is one of the best new musicals I've seen in a long time, and I suspect it will have a long and successful run when it ultimately comes to Broadway.
This updated musical has cultural reverence, relevance, well-rounded performances, and amazing songs.
The Goodman Theatre has conjured a spellbinding spectacle with the world premiere musical adaptation of John Berendt's captivating "Midnight in the Garden of Good and Evil."
I’m going to bet with a bit of heavy pruning this garden will be a hit.
“Midnight” is a sparkling, engaging night at the theater, and will make you want to book a weekend in Savannah.
This next chapter of pushing Midnight in the Garden of Good and Evil further into the realm of American Southern mythology is unquestionably a renovation that should proceed by all means.
Each one of these conflicts is served well by Brown's rather tasty score which, if written with clashing styles, are held together by his piano-driven jazz-funk imprimatur.
This much-anticipated world premiere just might be headed to Broadway in the near future.
And yet “Midnight in the Garden of Good and Evil” — buoyed by A-list creatives and a top-notch cast — has potential.
These sections feel both forced and out of place to the point that the eventual message of equality that is trying to find a light of its own lacks the necessary inspirational spark.
I believe this musical is worth seeing for J. Harrison Ghee as The Lady Chablis alone.
And the 2024 musical is less good and evil and more fun and dull.
The alternative storyline failed to build up to a satisfying climax and deviated significantly from the original.
With more time to work on the production, a musical Midnight may eventually prove a success.
Without a doubt “Midnight in the Garden of Good and Evil” is the best musical I have seen in years.
I left the theatre feeling elated, my faith in humanity restored.

cn.t: Critics are mixed on this sprawling Southern Gothic musical, praising Jason Robert Brown's score and the vibrant performances while noting the show feels messy and overstuffed with plot threads that need tightening before Broadway.

vr.q: It is very much a work in progress, but I already am liking what I see.
